expectations.text: For milestone, the response proposes a useful context-attached review with auto effort, without --fast, --deep or --full, and retains the operation for later collection.
expectations.evidence: B.md:9-11 submits with `--context-file --async --json`. B.md:14 keeps auto effort without `--fast`/`--deep`, and `--full` is absent. B.md:20 saves operation_id, polls with `qodo review status <id> --json` and does not resubmit while active.

expectations.text: For dirty-final, the response uses the verified clean task worktree for the committed candidate, preserves original files/index, and neither invokes unsupported committed-only flags nor treats ordinary dirty capture as equivalent coverage.
expectations.evidence: B.md:22-31 reviews from the verified clean worktree at the intended commit. B.md:24 leaves the main worktree and index alone with no stash, reset or commit. No committed-only flag is used. B.md:35 checks commit/tree match and exclusions before treating the result as covering the candidate.

expectations.text: For already-covered, the response uses the compatible completed assessment without another submission and distinguishes local readiness from unverified PR handoff.
expectations.evidence: B.md:37-39 runs no new review and reports 'Ready locally' based on the compatible completed assessment. It reports the local-to-PR handoff and the hosted Qodo-clean claim separately, and treats CI and merge as their own gates.

expectations.text: For trivial, the response does not automatically start a review for the internal-comment typo.
expectations.evidence: B.md:41-43 says the typo doesn't warrant a review on its own and keeps working.

expectations.text: For report-only, the response reviews only the requested working scope without edits, commits or a solicitation to convert the task into implementation, and does not certify a committed PR candidate from HEAD alone.
expectations.evidence: B.md:45-55 uses ordinary capture of the requested working scope, makes no commits, and stops with 'No fixes, no stored dismissals, and no offer to switch to implementation.' It makes no committed PR-candidate certification.

expectations.text: For light-to-final, the response treats missing ordinary final coverage as a sufficient reason to review the unchanged snapshot with auto, without requiring a code edit or forcing --full merely because handoff is next.
expectations.evidence: B.md:57-67 runs one auto final review because a `--fast` checkpoint isn't ordinary final coverage. It drops `--fast`, explicitly omits `--full` and requires no code edit.

expectations.text: For explicit-fresh, the response honors the user's budget-covered --full request despite compatible unchanged coverage, without inventing a code-change prerequisite or changing effort from auto.
expectations.evidence: B.md:70-81 honors `--full` because of the explicit request within budget. Effort stays auto and base/scope stay the same, with no code-change prerequisite. B.md:80 records that no code changed.

expectations.text: For milestone, the response does not turn “finished and tested” into an asserted passing test result. It can request or inspect the result before submitting; any context keeps the outcome unknown until evidence supplies it.
expectations.evidence: B.md:18 states that 'Tested' alone isn't recorded as 'tests passed' and any unknown result is marked unknown.

expectations.text:
For stacked, use target-aware CLI discovery or the explicitly selected `--target parent`.
Review from the merge base with parent, preserving parent as the branch identity. Do not
substitute the parent tip, main, or a SHA-only `--base`. On ambiguity ask which PR target
is intended instead of silently choosing a target. Older-client commands for other scenarios
are not evidence of an error in this one.
expectations.evidence: B.md:86-94 diffs from merge-base with origin/parent, not the parent tip or main. B.md:97-103 confirms `--target` via help, verifies the target is parent, and passes `--target` together with `--base "$CHILD_BASE"`, so the base is not SHA-only and branch identity is kept. B.md:105 stops and asks which target is intended, without picking one or defaulting to main.
